quarrelsome

KWOR-el-sum · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Quarrelsome is likely to argue or fight, especially over small or unimportant things.

The office was quieter once the two quarrelsome interns were assigned to different floors.

Example

Ever since they were small, the sisters had been famously quarrelsome, squabbling over everything from whose turn it was to choose the movie to who got the last slice of pizza.

Quarrelsome means prone to arguing over small things -- the sisters aren't in a serious feud, just constantly bickering.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

argumentative: Argumentative means given to arguing -- quick to push back and contradict in any discussion. Quarrelsome narrows the picture: a quarrelsome person doesn't just argue points, they pick small fights, bickering over trifles like chores and leftovers. Argumentative is a debating habit; quarrelsome is a bickering temperament.

disputatious: Disputatious means inclined to dispute and debate -- a formal, almost lawyerly readiness to contest claims and split hairs. Quarrelsome is homier and pettier: quarrelsome people squabble over small everyday things rather than contesting ideas. A disputatious scholar challenges arguments; a quarrelsome roommate fights about chores.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

agreeable: willing to go along with others

harmonious: free from conflict; getting along well

Where it sits · how ready to start arguments

disagreeable → quarrelsome → hostile

disagreeable vs. quarrelsome: Disagreeable is milder than quarrelsome -- a disagreeable person is unpleasant and hard to please, but a quarrelsome person goes further and actually starts the arguments.

hostile vs. quarrelsome: Hostile describes open, unfriendly opposition -- a stronger and more serious state than everyday quarrelsome bickering.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — quarrel: a dispute or argument (Latin querela)

suffix — -some: tending to be, or full of (Old English -sum)

Put it together: Quarrelsome comes from quarrel (a dispute, from Latin querela) + -some ('tending to be') -- literally 'tending to argue.'

Use the root in a new word: wholesome: The community center offers wholesome after-school activities for kids.

Root Check

Word Choice

Quarrelsome describes a personality prone to small, everyday arguments -- milder than irascible (a short temper and quickness to real anger) and very different from bellicose (an aggressive readiness for actual conflict or war, often used for nations or leaders).
